newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer but direction unclear.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer but direction unclear.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures ended the TIFFE day session on Friday slightly firmer amid a lack of market direction.
"The December has been caught in a narrow range of between 98.90 and 98.95 for most of this week, and it kept within that range today," said a dealer at a commercial bank.
The December settled at 98.95, up 0.02, mainly on pre-weekend short-covering. It moved between 98.92 and 98.96.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) said Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs) grew 3.1 percent in April from a year ago. This compared with economists' forecast of a rise of slightly below three percent.

Traders said the market paid little attention to the higher-than-expected rise in April money supply because a senior BOJ official said after the release of the data that the growth in M2+CDs in April was due to an increase in CDs. He also said that the growth did not seem to have been affected by the rise in Japan's sales tax on April 1.
